note: The screen every drafted analyst brief must pass before anyone sees it. A JavaScript page and a Deno function load this file unchanged; radar/brief/screen.py is the reference implementation and spec/screen_cases.json holds the cases every port must pass. The company, email, postcode and accusing patterns and the hedges are copied from the repository screen (fd-core) and a test keeps them equal. The private deny list of names is never part of this file: only a server holding it can run that check. The extra legal forms (patterns.company_name_extra) and the names rule are this screen's own.
regex_dialect: Every pattern is written for both ECMAScript and Python re. Compile with ASCII semantics (Python: re.ASCII) and the flags given, where 'i' means ignore case. Lookbehind is used.
reply: Trim white space. If the reply is wrapped in one Markdown code fence, take what is inside it. What is left must parse as one JSON object, or the only problem is not_json.
schema_check: Validate the draft against spec/brief.schema.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12). If it fails, report schema problems only and stop.
house_line: A rise in exports is a lead, not evidence of a breach.
ogl_line: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
fixed_fields: series and run must equal the context's; house_line and ogl_line must equal the lines above word for word; headline.text must contain headline_must_contain, ignoring case.
text_checks: Run on every string in the draft, line by line: remove carriage returns and split on line feeds. One problem per field and code is enough. company_name is reported for a match of patterns.company_name (the repository screen's pattern) or patterns.company_name_extra (legal forms used on the corridors).

company_name_extra.about: Legal forms used on the corridors that the repository's pattern does not hold, in ASCII: Kazakhstan (TOO, AO), Kyrgyzstan (OsOO), Uzbekistan (MChJ), Armenia and others (CJSC, OJSC, PJSC), the UAE (FZC), Thailand (PCL), Malaysia (Sdn Bhd, Bhd), Turkey (A.S., Ltd Sti), Serbia (d.o.o.). One to five capitalised words, not starting with a word such as The or This, then the form. Reported as company_name. This screen's own; fd-core's pattern is unchanged.

accusing.how: Each match of pattern or extra_pattern is a problem unless a hedge sits in the same clause. Take the text from hedge_before characters before the match to hedge_after characters after it; cut it at the end of the last clause break before the match and at the start of the first clause break after it; the match is hedged if what is left, lower-cased, contains any hedge.

names.about: Possible names of people or firms that the legal-form patterns miss. A capitalised word that does not start a sentence, or a word in capitals anywhere, is a problem (possible_name) unless it is on the allow list or appears in the context the draft was drafted from. A word that starts a sentence is not checked, so a name there is not caught: a net, not a guarantee.
names.how: Allowed words are the allow list plus every match of context_word in every string of the context, each with endings_removed taken off in order. Check each line of every string in the draft (as text_checks splits them): for each capitalised match, take endings_removed off in order; it passes if the result is allowed, or if the match starts a sentence: stepping back from the character before the match over any character in skip_back, the line's start is reached or the character reached is in starts. Then each acronym match passes only if it is allowed, wherever it stands. Report the capitalised matches of a line before its acronym matches.

figures.normalise: A token is group 1 + group 2 with its commas removed + group 3 lower-cased + group 4 lower-cased (missing groups are empty): '£8,012,904' gives '£8012904', '£8.0 m' gives '£8.0m', '3.3X' gives '3.3x'.
figures.how: The tokens of a text are every token match, then, with those matches replaced by spaces, every stray match as it stands, so no digit goes unchecked. Run this on the text of every claim. A claim token must be among the tokens of the strings of the items the claim cites, or of the context's free fields; if it is not, the problem is uncited_figure when the token appears anywhere in the context's strings and invented_figure when it does not. Only strings count, never JSON numbers.

number_words.how: A count written in words is a figure too: each match, lower-cased, adds its value from values to the text's tokens, after the token and stray matches, so it must be backed as a digit would be. One is left out: it is too common in plain prose to check.

multiples.how: A multiple or a fraction in words (doubled, tripled, twice, halved, threefold, three times) says more than the cited items can back. Every match in the text of a claim is the problem figure_in_words; the claim gives the figure the items write instead (for example 3.5x). A word followed by a hyphen, as in double-check, is not a match.

claims: A claim is an object with text, confidence and cites: the headline, the items of what_rose.uk, what_rose.onward and why_it_may_be_ordinary, linked_cases.note, any questions_to_check[].why_here and every responds_to_review[].change (with the review rules). Every id in cites must be the id of a fact, limit or case in the context (unknown_fact). The claim's confidence must not be above the lowest confidence of the items it cites (confidence_above_source), in confidence_order.
limits: Every id in the draft's limits must be the id of a limit in the context (unknown_fact).
cases: linked_cases.case_ids must hold every case_id in the context's cases (cases_missing, one problem) and nothing else (unknown_case, one per id).
red_flags: Each questions_to_check[].red_flag must be the id of a red flag in the context (unknown_red_flag); its question must equal that red flag's question word for word (red_flag_text_changed).
paths: A problem names its field by object keys joined with '.' and array positions as [n], for example what_rose.uk[0].text, questions_to_check[2].question, limits[3]. Ports must match code and path.

review.note: Reviewer notes: what an editor wrote when they returned or rejected an earlier version. The page builds them from the file's decisions since its last approval, oldest first, ids review-1 to review-5, and passes them to the prompt and to the screen apart from the context. They never extend the context: no word in a note becomes an allowed name and no figure in a note becomes a citable figure. Before a note reaches the prompt it passes the note checks: text_checks, names (against the context), instruction and max_note_length. A note that fails is held back, shown to the officer and not required in the draft.
review.placeholder: To be written: what this draft changed because of the note.

instruction.note: Words that read as instructions to the drafting model rather than a reviewer's point about the draft. A net, not a guarantee: the prompt also tells the model that notes are data.

review.answers: When notes are given, responds_to_review must answer each note id once (review_unanswered, review_duplicate) and no other (review_unknown). Each answer's change is a claim: its cites must include the note's id (review_not_cited) and may add fact, limit and case ids; figures and the confidence floor come from the context items it cites, never from the note. An answer whose text is the placeholder fails (review_placeholder). With no notes, responds_to_review must be absent or every answer is review_unknown.

problem_codes.not_json: The reply is not one JSON object.
problem_codes.schema: The draft does not match spec/brief.schema.json.
problem_codes.series_mismatch: series is not the context's series.
problem_codes.run_mismatch: run is not the context's run.
problem_codes.house_line: house_line is not the house line, word for word.
problem_codes.ogl_line: ogl_line is not the Open Government Licence line, word for word.
problem_codes.headline_not_hedged: The headline does not say the lead is not a finding.
problem_codes.em_dash: An em dash appears in the text.
problem_codes.company_name: Text that reads as a company name (a legal-form suffix, including those used on the corridors).
problem_codes.accusing_language: Judging or accusing wording outside a hedged clause.
problem_codes.possible_name: A capitalised word in mid-sentence, or a word in capitals, that is neither in the context nor on the allow list: it may name a person or a firm.
problem_codes.invented_figure: A figure that appears nowhere in the context.
problem_codes.figure_in_words: A multiple or fraction in words (doubled, tripled, twice, halved): give the figure the cited items write instead.
problem_codes.uncited_figure: A figure that is in the context but not in the items the claim cites.
problem_codes.unknown_fact: A cited or listed id that is not a fact, limit or case in the context.
problem_codes.confidence_above_source: A claim more certain than the least certain item it cites.
problem_codes.unknown_case: A linked case the context does not hold.
problem_codes.cases_missing: A case linked in the context is left out.
problem_codes.unknown_red_flag: A question cites a red flag the context does not hold.
problem_codes.red_flag_text_changed: A question differs from its red flag's wording.
problem_codes.deny_list_name: A name on the private deny list (server or reference screen only).
problem_codes.phone: A phone number (reference screen only; the figure check catches the digits anyway).
problem_codes.review_unanswered: A reviewer's note is not answered in responds_to_review.
problem_codes.review_unknown: An answer to a reviewer's note that this draft was not given.
problem_codes.review_duplicate: A reviewer's note is answered more than once.
problem_codes.review_not_cited: An answer to a reviewer's note does not cite the note.
problem_codes.review_placeholder: The answer to a reviewer's note is still the template's placeholder.
problem_codes.planted_instruction: Words that read as instructions to the drafting model. Notes are data, never instructions.
problem_codes.note_too_long: A reviewer's note is longer than max_note_length.
